```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# Run from the project root regardless of RStudio's knit-directory setting.
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = here::here())
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

```{r load, include=FALSE}
source("setup.R")

# TEMPORARY: get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) doesn't drop the new "consecutive" source type yet
# (park-run systems that buy piped water). Remove this filter once npswavacore's
# get_wsd() excludes it along with municipal, hauled, tribal, and purchased.
water_supplies <- get_wsd(rapid = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(coalesce(source_type, "") != "consecutive")

treatment <- calc_treatment_capacity_sensitivity(water_supplies)

# The same calculation with no coastal sources, to see what the reverse osmosis rule changes
no_coast_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write_csv(tibble(wsd_source_id = character(), coast_dist_m = numeric()), no_coast_file)
treatment_no_coast <- calc_treatment_capacity_sensitivity(water_supplies, coast_geometry = no_coast_file,
                                                          verbose = FALSE)

treatment <- treatment |>
  left_join(select(treatment_no_coast, wsd_source_id, score_without_coastal_rule = raw_treatment_capacity),
            by = "wsd_source_id") |>
  mutate(score = factor(raw_treatment_capacity, levels = 0:5))

# Results with source locations, for maps
treatment_sf <- water_supplies |>
  distinct(wsd_source_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(wsd_source_id) |>
  inner_join(treatment, by = "wsd_source_id")

show_table <- function(data, height = NULL, ...) {
  table <- data |>
    kable(digits = 2, format.args = list(big.mark = ","), ...) |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
  if (is.null(height)) table else scroll_box(table, height = height)
}

# 0 = least treatment capacity (most sensitive)
score_colors <- c("0" = "#8C2B0E", "1" = "#CB7223", "2" = "#DFCB34",
                  "3" = "#9BBF85", "4" = "#289A84", "5" = "#1F5F8B")

score_map <- function(data, label) {
  data <- mutate(data, score = droplevels(score))
  mapview(data, zcol = "score", layer.name = label, map.types = "Esri.WorldTopoMap",
          col.regions = unname(score_colors[levels(data$score)]))
}
```

## Purpose

This indicator scores how much treatment capacity each water supply has, from
**0 (no or unknown treatment)** to **5 (full treatment train for its source type)**.
Systems with more treatment can better handle the water quality changes that climate
change may bring, such as more turbidity after fire or floods, warmer water, and
saltwater intrusion. So a higher score means **lower sensitivity**, and the `norm_`
and `rank_` columns are inverted (higher = more sensitive).

The method comes from Lynette Schwanger's exploration
(`NPS_WSD/archive/exploration/NPS_WSD_Treatment_Indicator.Rmd`), adapted to the rapid
water supply list and conventions. With the same coastal flag, the function reproduces
her scores for every source it scores. The changes from her version are:

- It uses `get_wsd(rapid = TRUE)`, so municipal, purchased, hauled, tribal, and
  consecutive sources aren't included.
- Inactive, non-potable, and proposed sources aren't scored. Temporarily inactive
  sources are scored, since they're recent or possibly temporary closures.
- Coastal sources are identified with the rapid `coast_dist_m` (source within 50 km of
  the NOAA CUSP shoreline), instead of park centroids within 50 km of the TIGER coastline.
- Unknown treatment scores 0, as before, but is flagged in `treatment_unknown`.

## Step 1: Which sources are scored

Every rapid source is returned. Sources that can't be scored get `NA` with the reason
in `score_note`.

```{r step1}
treatment |>
  mutate(Status = coalesce(score_note, "Scored")) |>
  count(Status, name = "Sources") |>
  arrange(Status != "Scored", desc(Sources)) |>
  show_table()
```

## Step 2: Map treatments to categories

`treatment_system_type` can list several treatments. Each one is mapped to one or more
treatment categories:

```{r step2-map}
category_lookup <- enframe(treatment_category_lookup(), name = "Treatment type", value = "Categories")

treatment_counts <- treatment |>
  filter(!is.na(treatment_system_type)) |>
  separate_rows(treatment_system_type, sep = "[,;]") |>
  mutate(treatment_system_type = str_squish(treatment_system_type)) |>
  count(`Treatment type` = treatment_system_type, name = "Rapid sources")

category_lookup |>
  left_join(treatment_counts, by = "Treatment type") |>
  mutate(`Rapid sources` = replace_na(`Rapid sources`, 0L)) |>
  arrange(Categories, `Treatment type`) |>
  show_table(height = "450px", caption = "Treatment category map")
```

```{r step2-categories}
treatment |>
  filter(is.na(score_note), !treatment_unknown) |>
  separate_rows(treatment_category, sep = ",\\s*") |>
  count(Category = treatment_category, name = "Sources") |>
  arrange(desc(Sources)) |>
  show_table(caption = "Treatment categories on scored sources")
```

**Check:** treatment types that aren't in the category map are listed here. They're
ignored in scoring, and the function warns about them.

```{r step2-unmatched}
unmatched <- treatment |>
  filter(str_detect(coalesce(treatment_category, ""), "unmatched"))

if (nrow(unmatched) == 0) {
  cat("None: every treatment type on the rapid list is in the category map.")
} else {
  unmatched |> select(wsd_source_id, treatment_system_type) |> show_table()
}
```

## Step 3: Score by source type

Groundwater and surface water need different treatment trains, so each source is scored
on a track. GWUDI (groundwater under the direct influence of surface water), spring,
and rainwater sources are scored on both tracks and keep the higher score.

```{r step3-rules}
tribble(
  ~Score, ~Groundwater, ~`Surface water`,
  "5", "Oxidation + filtration + disinfection + an add-on (sediment, contaminant, pH, or corrosion)",
       "Sediment removal + filtration + disinfection + an add-on (oxidation, contaminant, pH, or corrosion)",
  "4", "Oxidation + filtration + disinfection", "Sediment removal + filtration + disinfection",
  "3", "Filtration + disinfection", "Filtration + disinfection",
  "2", "Filtration or disinfection", "Filtration or disinfection",
  "1", "Only emergency, oxidation, sediment, contaminant, pH, or corrosion treatment", "Same",
  "0", "Untreated or unknown", "Untreated or unknown"
) |>
  show_table(caption = "Scores 4 and 5 also need reverse osmosis if the source is coastal (Step 4)")
```

```{r step3-tracks}
treatment |>
  filter(is.na(score_note)) |>
  count(Track = scoring_track, `Source type` = source_type, name = "Sources") |>
  show_table()
```

## Step 4: Coastal sources need reverse osmosis

Coastal sources face saltwater intrusion, so they need reverse osmosis (RO) to score
4 or 5. A coastal source with a full treatment train but no RO scores 3. A source is
coastal if it's within 50 km of the NOAA CUSP shoreline (`coast_dist_m` from
`process_coastal_geometry()`, the same input as the storm surge and saltwater intrusion
indicators).

```{r step4-counts}
treatment |>
  filter(is.na(score_note)) |>
  summarize(`Coastal sources` = sum(coastal),
            `With reverse osmosis` = sum(coastal & has_reverse_osmosis),
            `Lowered by the coastal rule` = sum(raw_treatment_capacity < score_without_coastal_rule)) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r step4-lowered}
treatment |>
  filter(raw_treatment_capacity < score_without_coastal_rule) |>
  transmute(Source = wsd_source_id, Park = park_unit, `Source type` = source_type,
            Treatment = treatment_system_type,
            `Distance to coast (km)` = coast_dist_m / 1000,
            Score = raw_treatment_capacity, `Score without coastal rule` = score_without_coastal_rule) |>
  show_table(caption = "Sources whose score was lowered by the coastal rule")
```

```{r step4-map}
mapview(filter(treatment_sf, is.na(score_note), coastal),
        zcol = "has_reverse_osmosis", layer.name = "Coastal sources: reverse osmosis",
        map.types = "Esri.WorldTopoMap", col.regions = c("#8C2B0E", "#1F5F8B"))
```

## Results

```{r results-counts}
treatment |>
  filter(is.na(score_note)) |>
  count(Score = raw_treatment_capacity, Track = scoring_track) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Track, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(treatment |> filter(is.na(score_note)) |> count(Score = raw_treatment_capacity, name = "All sources"),
            by = "Score") |>
  show_table(caption = "Scored sources by treatment capacity score and track")
```

```{r results-map}
score_map(filter(treatment_sf, is.na(score_note)), "Treatment capacity score")
```

### Unknown treatment

These sources have no `treatment_system_type` in the WSD (blank or "U"), so they score 0,
which assumes minimum treatment capacity. Leaving them `NA` would count as zero
vulnerability in `calc_vulnerability_index()`, the same as the best-treated systems.
Filling in the WSD would improve these scores.

```{r unknown-map}
score_map(filter(treatment_sf, treatment_unknown), "Unknown treatment (scored 0)")
```

```{r unknown-parks}
treatment |>
  filter(treatment_unknown) |>
  count(Park = park_unit, Classification = classification, name = "Sources") |>
  arrange(desc(Sources)) |>
  show_table(height = "350px", caption = "Sources with unknown treatment by park")
```

## Distribution of indicator values

```{r dist-setup}
scored <- filter(treatment, is.na(score_note))

bar_color <- "#1F5F8B"

dist_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_text(color = "grey30"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0))

score_counts <- scored |> count(raw_treatment_capacity)
pct <- function(scores) round(100 * mean(scored$raw_treatment_capacity %in% scores))

park_scores <- scored |>
  group_by(park_unit) |>
  summarize(mean_score = mean(raw_treatment_capacity), sources = n(),
            unknown_share = mean(treatment_unknown))

score_2 <- filter(scored, raw_treatment_capacity == 2)
disinfection_only_pct <- round(100 * mean(str_detect(score_2$treatment_category, "disinfection") &
                                            !str_detect(score_2$treatment_category, "filtration")))
```

The score is ordinal with only six values, so its distribution is shown as counts per
score. It is strongly concentrated: score 2 (filtration *or* disinfection; `r disinfection_only_pct`% of these
are disinfection alone) holds `r pct(2)`% of scored sources, `r pct(0)`% score 0, and only
`r pct(4:5)`% reach 4 or 5. Because `norm_treatment_capacity` is a linear rescale of the
score, it has the same shape, just relabeled from 1.0 (score 0) to 0.0 (score 5).

```{r dist-raw, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(score_counts, aes(x = factor(raw_treatment_capacity), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = bar_color, width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, color = "grey20") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Treatment capacity score (0 = none or unknown, 5 = full train)",
       y = "Scored sources",
       title = "Most sources score 2: disinfection without filtration") +
  dist_theme
```

### By scoring track and unknown treatment

Surface water sources score higher than groundwater, because most surface systems
have both filtration and disinfection while most groundwater systems only disinfect.
The score-0 bar is mostly unknown treatment rather than confirmed untreated sources.

```{r dist-track, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 4}
scored |>
  mutate(track = factor(scoring_track, levels = c("Groundwater", "Surface water", "Both (higher score)"))) |>
  count(track, raw_treatment_capacity) |>
  complete(track, raw_treatment_capacity = 0:5, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(raw_treatment_capacity), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = bar_color, width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ track, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Treatment capacity score", y = "Scored sources",
       title = "Score distribution by scoring track (y-axes differ)") +
  dist_theme
```

```{r dist-unknown}
scored |>
  filter(raw_treatment_capacity == 0) |>
  count(Reason = if_else(treatment_unknown, "Unknown treatment", "Listed as untreated"),
        name = "Sources scoring 0") |>
  show_table()
```

### By park

Scores summarized per park, using each park's mean score across its scored sources.
The tall bar (2 to 2.25) is mostly parks where every scored source scores 2 (`r sum(park_scores$mean_score == 2)` parks), matching the source-level pattern; parks well below 2 usually
have many unknown or untreated sources.

```{r dist-park, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(park_scores, aes(x = mean_score)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0, closed = "left", fill = bar_color, color = "white", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:5, limits = c(0, 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(x = "Mean treatment capacity score per park", y = "Parks",
       title = paste0("Park mean scores (", nrow(park_scores), " parks)")) +
  dist_theme
```

```{r dist-park-low}
park_scores |>
  filter(mean_score < 1) |>
  arrange(mean_score) |>
  transmute(Park = park_unit, `Scored sources` = sources,
            `Mean score` = mean_score, `Unknown treatment (%)` = 100 * unknown_share) |>
  show_table(caption = "Parks with a mean score below 1")
```

## Checks

```{r checks}
scored <- filter(treatment, is.na(score_note))

tibble(
  Check = c("One row per rapid source",
            "Scores are whole numbers from 0 to 5",
            "Inactive, non-potable, and proposed sources are NA",
            "Score 0 has the highest normalized value (most sensitive)",
            "Score 5 has the lowest normalized value (least sensitive)",
            "Unknown treatment only on scored sources"),
  Result = c(
    nrow(treatment) == n_distinct(water_supplies$wsd_source_id) & !any(duplicated(treatment$wsd_source_id)),
    all(scored$raw_treatment_capacity %in% 0:5),
    all(is.na(treatment$raw_treatment_capacity[!is.na(treatment$score_note)])),
    all(scored$norm_treatment_capacity[scored$raw_treatment_capacity == 0] == max(scored$norm_treatment_capacity)),
    all(scored$norm_treatment_capacity[scored$raw_treatment_capacity == 5] == min(scored$norm_treatment_capacity)),
    all(is.na(treatment$score_note[treatment$treatment_unknown]))
  )
) |>
  mutate(Result = if_else(Result, "Pass", "FAIL")) |>
  show_table()
```

Normalized and ranked values for each score. Ranks are percentiles, so many tied scores
share one rank and the top rank is below 100.

```{r checks-standardized}
scored |>
  group_by(Score = raw_treatment_capacity) |>
  summarize(Sources = n(),
            Normalized = first(norm_treatment_capacity),
            Rank = first(rank_treatment_capacity)) |>
  show_table()
```
